label: Tower defense / unit-placement defense (TD, anime-TD, wave defense)
provenance: Web research, not owner screenshots. Every row below was fetched over the network on 2026-09-20 — shipped-game wikis read through the MediaWiki parse API (Fandom's HTML is behind Cloudflare; the api.php endpoint is not), and Roblox DevForum threads read directly. No image, no Luau source and no asset is copied here; each row records where the claim was read and what construction it describes, so the claim can be checked.

references.source: https://tds.fandom.com/wiki/How_to_Play — Tower Defense Simulator (Paradoxum Games) official community wiki, fetched via https://tds.fandom.com/api.php?action=parse&page=How_to_Play&prop=wikitext on 2026-09-20. The richest single description of a shipped Roblox TD HUD found.
demonstrates: the in-match HUD is THREE readouts and nothing else competing with them: base health, current wave, wave timer — and they are one assembly, not three widgets. The wiki describes it as a single bar: 'The main bar is the amount of health you have... The left text is the current wave. The right text is the remaining amount of time for the wave to end/wave to start.'
base health is a NUMBER on a bar, default 100, and the number is mutable by perks and by map modifiers (a shown example reads 200) — so the bar must render an arbitrary max, never a hardcoded 100

skip-wave is a VOTE BOX that appears after a delay, with accept and decline, and a tally in 'cast/required' form — '0/2 means that 0 players have voted to skip the wave and 2 players are required' — not a plain Skip button

the tower hotbar is the LOADOUT, fixed at five slots (six in some events, fewer in some modes), and 'Each slot has a number in the top left corner, which shows which key on the keyboard you have to press to place down your towers' — the keybind digit is a badge in the slot's top-left, not a caption underneath

clicking a placed tower opens an upgrade box whose contents are, in order: the NEXT upgrade's name, level and icon plus the changes it brings; detection badges for hidden / lead / flying arranged AROUND the tower icon; a progress bar under the upgrade name showing how many upgrades remain (three to six depending on the tower); the upgrade cost ON the button, greyed out at last level
sell is a button carrying the refund AMOUNT, and the targeting selector sits immediately next to it with seven fixed modes — First (default), Last, Strongest, Weakest, Closest, Farthest, Random

under the tower's model preview in that same box sit three lifetime figures: total damage dealt, current level, total cash spent on the tower; current stats (damage, firerate, range, income) run down the RIGHT side of the box

placement legality is signalled in the 3D world, not in the UI: 'You can only place towers down if their primary range circle is white', other towers project red spots, and cliff spots highlight while a cliff tower is held

a tower can carry more than one range circle at once: white primary range, a RED deadzone circle that enemies inside cannot be targeted from (Rocketeer), and additional ORANGE circles for utility ranges (Necromancer, Engineer)
match modifiers render as a small icon row at the bottom-left of the screen
keybinds are the interaction, not a convenience: 1-6 pick a tower, Q cancel placement, R rotate placement, E upgrade, T upgrade the tower's bottom path, X sell, Q switch hotbar, F/B/H/J/K/L abilities
mobile is the SAME HUD plus a joystick, jump, run, emote and sticker buttons — the TD layout is not re-flowed for touch, it is augmented; and 'you need to double tap to select and place down towers'
the pre-match screen is a mode VOTE with a ready button under the modes that shortens the timer to five seconds, not a menu

references.source: https://tds.fandom.com/wiki/Time_Scale — Tower Defense Simulator wiki, fetched via api.php parse on 2026-09-20.
demonstrates: game speed is a set of DISCRETE STOPS, never a slider: 0x (full pause), 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, with 1x the default

0x is a first-class stop and is described as a reading aid — 'pauses the match entirely, preventing anything from moving, which can be useful to allow more time to react'. A speed control that only goes forward is missing half of what the convention is for.
the control is ENTITLEMENT-GATED and consumes a currency (Time Scale Tickets) — so the speed cluster needs a locked/unavailable state and a cost affordance, not just five toggles
background music is explicitly exempt from the time scale, so the control is a simulation-rate control and not an audio-rate control
with the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass the scale can be set to custom values beyond 2x — the ladder has an unbounded variant, so the widget should not hardcode five children

references.source: https://tds.fandom.com/wiki/Sandbox_Mode — Tower Defense Simulator wiki, fetched via api.php parse on 2026-09-20.
demonstrates: the keybind badge is bounded by the keyboard, not by the rail: 'any towers selected past the 6th will not have a hotkey, and will have to be placed by clicking their button' — slots 7+ render with no digit badge rather than with a fake one

the admin/sandbox surface is a left SIDEBAR of toggles over the live board (infinite cash, infinite towers, invincible, consumable cooldowns, time scale) — a TD config surface is a rail beside the match, never a modal that hides the path
the entity picker is split into named sections (Modern / Legacy) and hovering an entry surfaces its health and speed as a hover readout
right-click on an icon in the picker is the add/remove-from-loadout gesture, distinct from left-click which selects

references.source: https://allstartd.fandom.com/wiki/Controls — All Star Tower Defense wiki, fetched via api.php parse on 2026-09-20.
demonstrates: desktop placement is a two-step gesture: click the unit tile, DRAG the ghost across the map, click to commit — the ghost tracks the cursor between the two clicks
the same hotbar key or the same tile, pressed a second time, is the CANCEL — cancellation is the selection gesture repeated, not a separate control

touch placement is a different interaction and needs different chrome: after tapping the unit and tapping the ground, 'you will see two options on the right of the screen (Place and Cancel)'. An explicit confirm/cancel PAIR appears on the RIGHT edge on touch and does not exist on desktop.
hotbar digits are 1 through 6 — the same six-slot ceiling as TDS, from an unrelated studio

references.source: https://allstartd.fandom.com/wiki/How_To_Play and https://allstartd.fandom.com/wiki/Beginners_Guide — All Star Tower Defense wiki, fetched via api.php parse on 2026-09-20.
demonstrates: the placed-tower surface is described as a CARD, not a window: 'When clicking/tapping on a tower, a card appears, which allows you to sell, upgrade, and see your tower's stats' — sell, upgrade and stats are the three obligatory regions

placement surfaces are typed and mutually exclusive: 'some units can only be placed on the ground, while others must be placed on high ground', so the legality tint has to answer a per-unit rule and not a global one
the loadout is six slots with the FIRST slot semantically special (leader), carrying a party-wide buff — the rail has a distinguished first cell rather than six identical cells
upgrades change abilities, not only numbers, so the upgrade card must have room for a named ability that is replaced, not merely a stat delta
the placement preview is a CLONE of the real tower model with a dedicated 'Collider' part at Transparency 0.5 — the ghost is the actual model made translucent, not a silhouette or an icon

validity is signalled by TINTING that collider: a green (BrickColor 'Sage green') fill for placeable and a red ('Really red') fill for blocked. The tint lives on the ghost, in the world, not as a banner in the ScreenGui.
minimum tower-to-tower spacing is enforced as a magnitude test — the thread's value is 6 studs — and breaching it is what flips the ghost red, so the red state has a spatial cause the player can see
placement is restricted to designated surfaces by name (a 'PlacePart'), so the buildable area is authored geometry and the ghost is legal only over it
left click commits, RIGHT CLICK cancels — the desktop cancel is the opposite mouse button, matching the keyboard cancel rather than replacing it
the range indicator is a 3D MESH lying on the ground, not a UI circle: a circular mesh of 65 vertices and 64 bones, one bone per sampled angle
64 segments is the practical fidelity ceiling — the author states it 'gets less precise after 64' — so a range ring is a 64-gon, and a radius parameter scales it rather than a new mesh being built

the ring can be occlusion-aware: raycasting outward along each bone and pulling bones inward where geometry blocks the shot turns the circle into the tower's actual reachable area rather than a decorative disc
glow is faked with a larger Neon clone behind the mesh, because Roblox will not render a Highlight over a transparent mesh — the outline has to be geometry or texture, it cannot be a stroke

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-did-they-do-this-ui/3097666 — Roblox DevForum, Art Design Support; the thread is specifically about reproducing Tower Defense Simulator's look. Fetched 2026-09-20.
demonstrates: the striped disc under a TDS tower is 'a cylinder with a texture on it' — the circular base marker is world geometry with a tiled texture, which is why it sits under the tower in perspective instead of floating flat like a ScreenGui frame

its outline is BAKED INTO THE IMAGE, not stroked: the replies note the outline 'is part of the image itself (as it doesn't render over the tower)'. A UIStroke-style outline on a world marker is the wrong mechanism and reads wrong.

two engine constraints force that choice and a generator must know them: a Highlight will not show on a transparent part, and a place may have at most 32 Highlights alive at once — so per-tower selection outlines cannot be Highlights in a game with dozens of towers
the flat panels in the same game are described as 'a box with a UI stroke that has a UIGradient' — the panel stroke is not a flat colour, it is a gradient run along the stroke itself

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/feedback-needed-for-td-upgrade-ui/3295956 — Roblox DevForum, Art Design Support, fetched 2026-09-20.
demonstrates: the upgrade card is laid out VERTICALLY and split into a left region and a right region; the developer's redesign kept the vertical orientation and the split, changing only styling
the obligatory contents named are tower name, tower image, stats block, upgrade control — and a rank/tier marker, whose placement was the whole design problem

the resolution offered for the rank marker was either the very top of the left-hand region or folded into the name line as 'Name - X1' — tier is a prefix or a corner badge on the identity block, never a fifth column
the thread exists because a card that fits the rest of the game's UI beat the card the developer preferred in isolation; the card is subordinate to the HUD's language

references.source: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/tower-defense-gui-feedback/2338468 — Roblox DevForum, Creations Feedback, fetched 2026-09-20. Recorded for the failure modes, which are the ones a generator reproduces by default.
demonstrates: the first thing a critic named was mixed typefaces — 'too much font changing... Go for one uniform font'. One face across the whole HUD is a rule, not a preference.
the second was mixing image assets with emoji glyphs in the same icon run; an icon set must be one kind of thing

the third was spacing: the card read 'too compact', the stats title collided with the upgrade rows, and the developer's correction then over-spaced — so the card needs an explicit, uniform gutter rather than per-element nudges
the specialist/upgrade list at the bottom of the card was CUT OFF and needed to scroll — the upgrade list is variable-length and must be authored as a scrolling region, not a fixed stack
icon-only stats were unreadable — 'couldn't understand the last one. AT ALL' — every stat row needs a text label beside its icon

references.source: https://thenerdstash.com/how-to-play-toilet-tower-defense-beginners-guide/ — beginner's guide to Toilet Tower Defense (Telanthric Development), fetched 2026-09-20. Corroborating rather than primary: it confirms the rail and the upgrade ladder but does not give positions for the other HUD elements, and is recorded at that weight.
demonstrates: the unit rail runs along the BOTTOM of the screen and placement starts by clicking a tile in it — the same rail position as TDS and ASTD, from a third studio

every tile carries its own cost, and the match opens with a small fixed budget (300) that most tiles are already unaffordable against — the affordability state is the rail's normal condition, not an edge case

the upgrade ladder is short and bounded (up to Level 3 in this game) and each step moves three stats at once: damage, range and attack cooldown — the upgrade card's delta region has roughly three rows, not twenty

rules.note: Distilled from the references above. Units are Roblox UI units — px for stroke and radius, studs for world distances, scale-relative for placement. Anything inherited from simulator.json rather than observed for this genre is marked inherited:true, because a rule nobody checked in this genre is a guess wearing a number.

hudTriad.rule: The in-match HUD is exactly three readouts, and base health, wave number and wave timer are ONE assembly, not three widgets: a health bar across the top centre with the wave number set at its LEFT end and the countdown at its RIGHT end.
hudTriad.never: three separate corner-anchored panels for health, wave and timer
hudTriad.why: TDS describes the whole thing as 'the main bar' with left text and right text. Splitting it into three corners is the single most common way a generated TD HUD stops reading as a TD HUD.

cashReadout.rule: Match cash is its own pill, separate from the health/wave assembly, and is the value the tower rail and every cost label are compared against.
cashReadout.position: near the tower rail, not in the health assembly
cashReadout.why: Cash changes on every kill and every purchase; parking it inside the wave bar makes the one number the player watches while placing sit at the opposite end of the screen from the rail they are placing from.

towerRail.rule: A horizontal rail of square tower tiles along the BOTTOM of the screen. Slot count is the LOADOUT size, fixed for the match — five or six — not the size of the player's inventory.
towerRail.costLabel: every tile carries its placement cost
towerRail.why: TDS (five slots, digit in the top-left corner), ASTD (six, first slot is the leader) and Toilet Tower Defense (bottom rail, cost per tile) agree across three studios. TDS also states outright that slots past the sixth get NO hotkey, so slot 7+ renders with no badge rather than a fabricated one.

affordability.rule: An unaffordable tile DIMS and its cost label goes red; the tile is never removed, never reordered, and never hidden.
affordability.why: Toilet Tower Defense opens with 300 against a rail most of whose tiles cost more. The rail's job early in a match is to show the player what they are saving toward, so the unaffordable state is the default state and must stay legible.

placementPreview.rule: The preview is a CLONE of the real tower model with its collider at Transparency 0.5, following the pointer ray. Validity is a TINT ON THE GHOST — green placeable, red blocked — never a banner, toast or text warning in the ScreenGui.
placementPreview.surfaceIsAuthored: placement is legal only over named buildable geometry, and the legality rule is per-tower-type (ground vs cliff/high-ground)
placementPreview.why: The DevForum placement system tints a 0.5-transparency collider sage green / really red at a 6-stud spacing test; TDS states placement is legal only while the primary range circle is white and that other towers project red spots. Two independent sources put the answer in the world, on the model. A generated TD that prints 'Invalid placement' in a label has moved the feedback to where the player is not looking.

placementGesture.desktop: click the tile (or press its digit) → ghost follows the cursor → LEFT CLICK commits
placementGesture.desktopCancel: right click, the Q key, or pressing the same tile/digit a second time — all three cancel
placementGesture.touch: tap the tile → tap the ground → an explicit PLACE / CANCEL button pair appears on the RIGHT EDGE of the screen and commits or aborts
placementGesture.why: ASTD documents the re-press-to-cancel gesture and the touch-only Place/Cancel pair on the right; the DevForum system uses right-click to cancel; TDS binds Q to cancel and R to rotate and says mobile requires a double tap. The touch confirm pair is the rule a generator will miss: on touch the commit cannot be the same tap as the aim.

rangeIndicator.rule: The range ring is WORLD GEOMETRY lying on the ground under the tower — a ~64-segment circular mesh, or a cylinder with the ring baked into its texture — not a UI circle and not a Highlight.
rangeIndicator.outline: baked into the texture or built as a larger Neon clone behind the mesh

channels.red: deadzone — enemies inside cannot be targeted
channels.orange: secondary or utility range (buff aura, repair radius)

rangeIndicator.shownWhen: while a tower is held for placement, and while a placed tower is selected
rangeIndicator.engineConstraints: a Highlight will not render over a transparent part, and a place may hold at most 32 Highlights at once — so per-tower selection outlines must be geometry or texture
rangeIndicator.why: The FOV resource is a 65-vertex / 64-bone mesh and says precision stops improving past 64; the TDS-reproduction thread says the disc is a textured cylinder whose outline is part of the image. TDS itself documents three simultaneous ring colours on one tower. A single flat white circle drawn in a ScreenGui fails all three.

upgradePopover.rule: Clicking a placed tower opens a side-anchored CARD, never a centred modal — the path and the enemies must stay visible while the player upgrades.
upgradePopover.anchor: screen edge beside the tower, board stays uncovered
upgradePopover.orientation: vertical, split into an identity/preview region and a stats region
regions: identity: tower name with its rank/tier as a prefix or a corner badge on the name line, and a live model preview
lifetime figures under the preview: total damage dealt, current level, total cash spent on this tower
detection badges — hidden / lead / flying — arranged AROUND the tower icon, not listed as text
next upgrade: its name, its level, its icon and the stat changes it brings
a segmented progress bar of upgrade steps remaining (3-6 steps is the normal range; short ladders of 3 also ship)
current stats down the right side: damage, firerate, range, income — each with a TEXT LABEL beside its icon
the action row: upgrade, sell, targeting
upgradePopover.upgradeList: authored as a SCROLLING region, because the number of upgrade rows varies per tower
upgradePopover.why: TDS's upgrade box is the fullest description found and every region above appears in it; the two DevForum feedback threads independently name the vertical left/right split, the tier-as-prefix resolution, the cut-off upgrade list that needed to scroll, and the icon-only stats nobody could read.

upgradeButton.rule: The upgrade button CARRIES ITS COST as its main text. At max level it greys out in place — it is never removed and never replaced by a different control.
upgradeButton.maxLevelState: greyed, still showing the ladder as complete
upgradeButton.why: TDS: 'The upgrade cost is also shown. You can click it to buy the upgrade. If the tower is on its last level, the upgrade button is greyed out.' A cost-less 'Upgrade' button makes the player open the card to learn a number they should have been able to read from it.

sellButton.rule: Sell carries the REFUND AMOUNT as a number, not the bare word Sell, and sits immediately beside the targeting selector.
sellButton.why: TDS: 'You can sell towers to remove them, but only get the stated amount of money back.' The refund is never the full spend, so the number is the whole decision.

targetingSelector.rule: A cycling selector adjacent to sell, with seven fixed modes in this order: First, Last, Strongest, Weakest, Closest, Farthest, Random. First is the default for every tower.
targetingSelector.why: Enumerated exactly in TDS. This set is a genre convention strong enough that a TD card without it reads as unfinished; inventing a different set reads as a different game.

waveProgression.rule: Waves are numbered from 0 and the inter-wave gap is a live countdown, not a Next Wave button. The early-start affordance is a VOTE BOX with a cast/required tally ('0/2'), offering accept and decline.
waveProgression.why: TDS: the skip box appears after a delay, needs the stated number of votes, and grants the wave reward early at the cost of the next wave starting early. A single-player Skip button drops the whole tension of the mechanic.

speedControl.rule: Discrete stops, never a slider: 0x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, with 1x pre-selected. 0x is a real stop and is a reading aid, not a pause menu.
speedControl.lockable: the cluster needs a locked/priced state — in TDS it consumes a ticket currency and is solo-only; an unbounded variant exists behind a gamepass, so the widget must not hardcode five children
speedControl.why: Enumerated on the TDS Time Scale page. The 0x stop is the one a generator omits and the one players use most for reading a crowded board.

modifierStrip.rule: Active match modifiers render as a small icon row at the BOTTOM-LEFT of the screen, with the detail on hover.
modifierStrip.why: TDS states the position outright. It is the one HUD region left for per-match state, and it stays out of the rail's way.

configRail.rule: Any in-match configuration surface (admin, sandbox, settings) is a rail down a screen EDGE over the live board, not a modal that hides the path.
configRail.why: The TDS sandbox admin panel is a sidebar of toggles with the match still running behind it. A TD match cannot be paused to read a menu unless the game has an explicit 0x stop, so its menus have to be edge-anchored.

typography.rule: ONE typeface across the entire HUD, every rail tile, every card and every readout. Numbers are the only thing allowed a different weight.
typography.iconography: one kind of icon — either all image assets or all glyphs, never mixed — and every stat icon gets a text label beside it
typography.why: Both DevForum feedback threads led with exactly these two faults. They are also the two faults a generator falls into by default, because it reaches for an emoji when it has no asset.

cardPadding.rule: One uniform gutter inside the upgrade card, applied at the container, not per-element nudges.
cardPadding.why: The GUI-feedback thread records the card reading 'too compact' with the stats title colliding with the upgrade rows, and then the correction over-spacing. Both failures come from spacing set element by element.

panelStroke.why: Inherited from simulator.json, with one genre-specific observation on top: the TDS-reproduction thread describes the panels as 'a box with a UI stroke that has a UIGradient', so in this genre the stroke itself carries a gradient rather than a flat colour. Thickness and colour role are not independently measured here and are carried over.

cornerRadius.why: Inherited from simulator.json. No tower-defense source read here states a radius, so these are carried rather than observed, and say so.

priceDisplay.rule: icon then number inside a pill
priceDisplay.why: Inherited from simulator.json. Consistent with every cost surface described in this genre (tile cost, upgrade cost, sell refund) but not independently measured for stroke or radius here.

limits: Fandom serves its article HTML behind Cloudflare, so the wiki rows were read through api.php as wikitext. That is the same content, but it means the SCREENSHOTS those pages embed were named and not seen — every wiki-derived claim above is a claim the page states in prose, never one inferred from an image nobody looked at.

No numeric stroke weight, corner radius or padding value was found in any tower-defense source read here. panelStroke, cornerRadius and priceDisplay are therefore carried from simulator.json and flagged inherited:true rather than restated as if this genre had confirmed them.

Tower Defense Simulator is over-weighted: three of eleven rows are its wiki, and it is the most thoroughly documented Roblox TD in existence, which is exactly why it is also the most likely to be mistaken for the genre. The rules above only promote a TDS detail to a rule where ASTD, Toilet Tower Defense or a DevForum thread agrees — the bottom rail, the six-slot ceiling, the ghost-tint placement feedback, the sell/upgrade/stats card. The seven targeting modes and the five speed stops are recorded as TDS-only conventions and named as such.
Nothing here has been rendered and compared. simulator.json earned its numbers by being built in Studio and looked at; this file has not had that pass, so it is research, not yet a verified profile.
